meta.title: Ipnoria — DNS, DHCP, IPAM, RADIUS and PKI in a single appliance
meta.description: Free and open-source DDI appliance: IPAM, DNS (BIND 9), DHCP (Kea), 802.1X network access (FreeRADIUS) and PKI (EJBCA), installed from an ISO and managed from a web console.

hero.title: DNS, DHCP, IPAM, RADIUS and PKI. One appliance.
hero.lead: Ipnoria installs from an ISO and replaces the address spreadsheet, the Windows DNS and DHCP servers, the NPS and AD CS. One web console drives it all, corporate Wi‑Fi included.

demo.soonText: Meanwhile, we'll show you the console on a video call, on your own cases: DHCP migration, 802.1X Wi‑Fi, cluster.

why.title: Your whole corporate network, in one place

items.title: One ISO, and it's installed
items.text: A single ISO (BIOS and UEFI) installs everything, with nothing downloaded on first boot. The same ISO upgrades an existing installation and keeps your data.

items.title: One source of truth
items.text: Allocating an address creates the DNS record (A/AAAA and PTR) and the DHCP reservation in the same transaction. Network templates apply scope, options and naming rule on creation.

items.title: Make mistakes safely
items.text: A restore point comes before every configuration change, deployment or import. An unconfirmed network change rolls itself back, and the database restores to a given minute.

items.title: Wi-Fi and VPN without NPS or AD CS
items.text: RADIUS driven from the console: access rules by Active Directory group, EAP-TLS, PEAP, EAP-TTLS and a second factor, with a simulation before deployment.

items.title: A built-in PKI
items.text: Authorities, revocation, SCEP for network devices, publication in Active Directory and workstation certificates issued automatically. The key stays on the workstation.

items.title: High availability end to end
items.text: Two data nodes and a witness. Database, DHCP, DNS, RADIUS and PKI follow the cluster, and switchover can be tested from the console.

items.title: Start from what you have
items.text: Import Windows Server DHCP and DNS exports, read Active Directory directly, import from NetBox or an existing NPS, and discover the network.

items.title: Secure by construction
items.text: Verified supply chain, unprivileged console, nftables firewall, encrypted secrets, full audit log, SIEM export, OpenID Connect SSO and API tokens.

why.lead: Every service is a proven open-source component. Ipnoria ties them together, so a change in one place is right everywhere.

gallery.title: The console, as it is
gallery.lead: Screenshots of the real console, with fictitious demonstration data. The console itself is available in English.

modules.title: What the console covers
modules.lead: HTTPS console in English and French, light and dark themes, keyboard-driven global search.

items.name: IPAM
items.text: Overlapping IP spaces, containers, networks and pools, VLANs, templates, naming rules, ghost addresses, network discovery, NetBox.

items.name: DNS
items.text: BIND 9: primary, secondary and forward zones, views, reverse zones, history with rollback, consistency checks, response rate limiting.

items.name: DHCP
items.text: Kea: scopes, ranges, reservations, client classes, leases and high availability.

items.name: DNS filtering
items.text: Query log, one-click allow and block lists, hosts and adblock lists, DNS tunnel detection.

items.name: Network access
items.text: FreeRADIUS: Wi-Fi, VPN and switch clients, Active Directory, EAP-TLS, PEAP, EAP-TTLS, second factor, authentication log.

items.name: PKI
items.text: EJBCA: authorities and CRLs, certificates, SCEP, publication in AD, workstation certificates, backup and updates.

items.name: Import and AD
items.text: Windows DHCP and DNS exports, zone transfer, LDAP, NetBox, NPS.

items.name: Cluster
items.text: Status, live settings, virtual address, dedicated network, guided switchover test.

items.name: System
items.text: 36 alert rules, scheduled backups, point-in-time restore, online updates with automatic rollback, firewall.

cluster.title: Two data nodes, one witness
cluster.text: PostgreSQL replicates with Patroni and etcd, Kea load-balances DHCP, BIND runs primary and secondary, and a virtual address follows the leader. Without a witness, a two-node cluster tolerates no failure: the witness holds no data, it only provides quorum.

blocks.title: Built on proven open-source components
blocks.lead: Ipnoria doesn't reinvent network daemons: it assembles, configures and monitors them.

privacy.title: Privacy
privacy.intro: This site sets no analytics or advertising cookies and loads nothing from third parties: fonts and images are served by the site itself.
privacy.cookie: Two preference cookies: “lang” remembers the language you chose, “theme” the display theme. They only serve to show the site the way you asked, and therefore require no consent.
privacy.form: The data you enter (name, email, organization, topic, message) is used only to answer your request. Legal basis: your consent. It is kept for {days} days and then deleted automatically.
privacy.ip: To limit abuse, a non-reversible fingerprint of your IP address is stored with the message. The address itself is never stored.
privacy.rights: You can request access to, correction or deletion of your data by writing to the address given in the legal notice. You can also lodge a complaint with the CNIL.
privacy.newsletter: If you subscribe, your email address is used only to announce new releases. It is used only after you confirm through a link sent by email; unconfirmed addresses are deleted after 7 days. Unsubscribing deletes it at once.
privacy.analytics: If enabled, statistics are measured by a self-hosted tool (Umami), without cookies or personal identifiers, and they honour your browser's Do Not Track setting. No data is passed to third parties.
privacy.votes: Your email address is used only to send the confirmation link. It is not kept: only a non-reversible fingerprint is stored to prevent duplicates. Unconfirmed votes are deleted after 7 days.
privacy.booking: Name, email address, organization and context are used only to organize the demo (confirmation, reminder the day before, cancellation). They are deleted 90 days after the meeting.
privacy.tools: The checklist, sizing calculator, DHCP import preview and subnet calculator run in your browser. What you enter and the files you drop are never sent; the checklist and the plan are kept in the browser's local storage.

sizing.topoCluster: Cluster: two data nodes and a witness

note.pki: The PKI runs in a Java container: 2 GB of memory are added.
note.radius: RADIUS is light; authentications per second matter more than the number of devices.
note.dnslog: Disk includes the DNS query log, proportional to the number of devices.
note.large: Beyond 30,000 devices, run a load test before settling the sizing.
note.relays: Several sites: each site's DHCP relays point to the appliance (or to both nodes of a cluster).
note.cluster: Plan a dedicated network between the three machines and a virtual address for the service.

sizing.disclaimer: An order of magnitude, to confirm with a test on your real load. Documented starting point: 2 vCPU, 4 GB, 40 GB.
